sources.title: Structured interview note preserving longest-substring requirement

claims.text: The strongest repository source explicitly requires finding the longest substring without repeated characters and returning the substring itself rather than only its length; Java, null behavior, Unicode unit, and equal-length tie-breaking are not source-proven.

Under the declared Java code-point and leftmost-tie contract, the sliding-window implementation preserves a duplicate-free window and matches independent quadratic-oracle results across fixed, exhaustive, and seeded-random cases, including stale-last-seen and supplementary-code-point boundaries.

The implementation materializes the input code points once and scans them with monotone window boundaries, so runtime is O(n) with O(n) worst-case auxiliary space for the code-point array plus last-seen map.

validation.command: compile exact candidate Solution.java; compile/run independent Reviewer.java against O(n^2) code-point oracle
validation.reported_stdout: PASS fixed=13 exhaustive=87381 random=10000 unicode-code-point=covered stale-last-seen=covered leftmost-tie=covered null=rejected

boundary_tests.expected: return the leftmost longest valid substring, including empty string
left boundary never moves backward and result matches oracle
leftmost longest substring abc is preserved
supplementary characters are treated as one code point and results match oracle

boundary_tests.case: all strings of length 0..8 over a,b,c,U+1F600
10,000 seeded random strings over ASCII, CJK, Euro, and supplementary code points
boundary_tests.expected: all outputs equal independent O(n^2) oracle
explicit IllegalArgumentException under declared reference contract

findings: Repository source requires the longest substring without repeated characters and explicitly requires returning the substring itself rather than only its length; Java, null behavior, Unicode unit, and equal-length tie-breaking are not source-proven.
Candidate labels Java, non-null input, Unicode code-point semantics, empty-string behavior, and leftmost tie-breaking as reference-contract choices instead of source facts.
The sliding-window invariant is sound: [left,right] contains no repeated code point, and the prev >= left guard prevents a stale last-seen index from moving the window backward.

An independent OpenJDK 21.0.11 oracle passes 13 fixed boundary cases, all 87,381 strings of length 0..8 over a four-symbol alphabet including a supplementary Unicode code point, and 10,000 seeded random cases; null rejection, stale-last-seen behavior, supplementary code points, and leftmost ties are covered.
The O(n) time and O(n) worst-case auxiliary-space claims match the shown implementation; the answer distinguishes code points from grapheme clusters and avoids fabricated project experience.
